segments.text: A block was devoted to the guided exercise. The data were organised in a table on the board, one example was worked through step by step and the most common mistakes were pointed out. The recommendation was to check every result against an independent estimate before accepting it. The session ended with a short reflection on how useful the method is in other contexts. Students were asked to note one concrete question to bring up in the next class.

The group worked on the group discussion in pairs. Each pair proposed a case and explained why its solution was valid; the proposals were then compared. The instructor insisted on justifying every decision and on distinguishing a hypothesis from a conclusion. Before leaving, each student wrote one conclusion on a card. The cards will be reviewed at the start of the next session to detect misunderstandings.

During the session a point worth retaining was introduced. Linear independence is defined as a set of vectors in which none can be written as a linear combination of the others. A short exercise was then solved and the result was checked against the initial estimate. The recommendation was to write down the complete procedure and review the units before submitting it. The closing included a three-item checklist to repeat at home. The checklist will be published together with the next exercise.

The explanation of the edge cases included a short proof and a counterexample. The counterexample showed why a rule cannot be applied mechanically. Before closing the block, students were asked to summarise the idea in one sentence and write down their main question. The last minutes were reserved for questions and a reminder of the next session's material. The instructor recommended revisiting the examples before attempting the new exercises.

The class revisited the final synthesis through a guided question. Students answered in turn and the instructor connected their contributions with earlier concepts. The block ended with a three-step checklist to avoid repeating the same mistakes in the next exercise. The session ended with a short reflection on how useful the method is in other contexts. Students were asked to note one concrete question to bring up in the next class.

The instructor paused on an idea that will appear in the exercises. The number of vectors in the base example is set to three in this course. The group discussed two possible applications and compared their advantages. It was stressed that a clear formulation matters as much as the final answer, especially when a decision has to be justified. Before leaving, each student wrote one conclusion on a card. The cards will be reviewed at the start of the next session to detect misunderstandings.

To close the assigned homework, the class summarised what had been learned and proposed an extension activity. The activity asked students to apply the concept in a new context and explain the limits of the approach. It was stressed that a clear procedure matters as much as the final result. The closing included a three-item checklist to repeat at home. The checklist will be published together with the next exercise.

The session began with a review of the review of the previous session. The instructor asked everyone to reconstruct the main argument without looking at their notes and then compare it with a partner. The differences were discussed and a shared definition was agreed before moving on. The last minutes were reserved for questions and a reminder of the next session's material. The instructor recommended revisiting the examples before attempting the new exercises.

The explanation formalised a central criterion for the topic. To solve a system by Gaussian elimination, the procedure is to order the equations and eliminate variables from the top down. An edge case was reviewed and it was explained why a mechanical application of the idea would lead to an error. The conclusion was to check the assumptions before using a formula. The session ended with a short reflection on how useful the method is in other contexts. Students were asked to note one concrete question to bring up in the next class.
